title: Systematic Review of Accountability in Pakistan's Polio Eradication Program
author: Imre Papp
materials: Import articles into analysis software (i.e., Quirkos) to facilitate systematic coding and organization of data.

steps.title: Search Databases
steps.instruction: Systematically search Embase (via Ovid), PubMed, SSCI (Social Science Citation Index), Scopus, and EconLit using specific search terms.

substeps.instruction: Use search terms related to: a) Pakistan (including province names) AND b) corruption or accountability or governance or integrity AND c) polio or poliomyelitis or "polio vaccine"

steps.title: Manage Search Results
steps.instruction: Process the search results based on satisfaction with the output.

substeps.instruction: If satisfied, save the search string, record the date of search, and download the RIS file of publications.
If not satisfied, refine the search and reassess before recording the search string.

steps.title: Import and De-duplicate Studies
steps.instruction: Upload RIS files containing search results to Covidence software for review.

substeps.instruction: Allow Covidence to automatically remove most duplicates.
Manually remove any remaining duplicates.

steps.title: Screen for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Assess eligibility based on title relevance using inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Apply inclusion criteria: research took place in Pakistan, relates to a polio eradication program, addresses program efficacy/accountability/corruption, written in English, and published between 2000 and 2026.

Apply exclusion criteria: research not in Pakistan or not relating to the polio program, studies assessing vaccine efficacy (rather than delivery program), articles not related to success/limitations of eradication efforts, not written in English, or published before 2000.
Ensure two independent reviewers complete the screening process and reach consensus via discussion if disagreements occur.

steps.title: Conduct Full-Text Review
steps.instruction: Perform a full-text review of remaining studies to determine final eligibility.

substeps.instruction: Search citations of reviewed articles for any further potentially relevant studies.

steps.title: Search Grey Literature
steps.instruction: Search the WHO, UNICEF, World Bank, and Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) databases for grey literature regarding polio governance, accountability, and/or corruption.

steps.title: Extract Descriptive Data
steps.instruction: Extract data from each included study into a spreadsheet with the following 15 fields: 1) title, 2) author, 3) year of publication, 4) country and setting of study, 5) aim of study, 6) study design, 7) start/end date, 8) population, 9) inclusion criteria, 10) # of participants, 11) identified themes/subthemes (for qualitative work), 12) important quotes (for qualitative work), 13) key findings/results summary, 14) limitations, 15) notes.

steps.title: Perform Thematic Synthesis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using Thomas and Harden's thematic synthesis approach.

substeps.instruction: Conduct iterative line-by-line coding on findings sections of each study, generating codes inductively.
Group codes into descriptive themes that capture recurring patterns using a constant comparative approach.
Develop analytical themes through interpretive analysis and research team discussion to generate higher-order insights.
Support key themes with illustrative participant quotes and maintain an audit trail of analytical decisions.

steps.title: Assess Methodological Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality and confidence of findings using standardized frameworks.

substeps.instruction: Use GRADE for quantitative findings and GRADE-CERQual for qualitative findings.

Assess qualitative studies using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) Qualitative Checklist across domains: study design, data collection, reflexivity, ethical considerations, and rigor of analysis.
Ensure quality appraisal is conducted independently by at least two reviewers, resolving disagreements through discussion.

steps.title: Evaluate Review Findings
steps.instruction: Evaluate each review finding across four domains to assign an overall confidence level (high, moderate, low, or very low) and produce a summary table.

substeps.instruction: Methodological limitations: concerns about design or conduct of primary studies.
Coherence: degree to which finding is grounded in and supported by data across studies.
Adequacy of data: richness and quantity of data supporting the finding.
Relevance: applicability of data to the review question and context.
